notes: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE. Every address, MAC and name here is a reserved documentation value (RFC 5737 addresses, an RFC 7042 MAC, example.invalid names) and matches no real network. Copy this file to ~/.machine/fleet-paths.json (or point PCAI_FLEET_PATHS at your copy) and replace the values with your own. Keep the real file out of the repository. tailnetV6 is optional: when a host records it, a MagicDNS name may also resolve to that one IPv6 address; without it, any IPv6 answer for the name is rejected. Test-FleetPath.ps1 reads it and never writes it. Candidate order is lan (listed order), then tailnet, then magicDns. A service's via list narrows that set.

gateways.name: router-subnet-a
gateways.notes: Read the MAC on a host where this address is the on-link default gateway (Get-NetNeighbor -IPAddress <ip>). A host that reaches the gateway by routing holds no neighbour row for it and cannot verify the entry.

gateways.name: router-subnet-b
gateways.notes: A router with an interface on a second subnet can show the same MAC on both. A foreign network that reuses your subnet answers at the same gateway address with a different MAC, so the MAC, not the subnet, proves you are home.

nas.notes: The tailnet peer name can differ from this key; peers are matched by tailnet address.

workstation.notes: ssh 2222 is the Windows sshd, ssh 22 is WSL. The message-bus hub listens on the tailnet only.

minipc.notes: Example of a LAN address that is blocked from one subnet, so the LAN candidate times out there and the tailnet carries the traffic.

router.notes: LAN only. It has no tailnet address, so it is unreachable off the home LAN.
